key_insight: A modular benchmarking framework cleanly separates quantum search-direction estimation from classical update rules to study how optimizers behave on parameterized quantum circuits under limited shots and evaluation budgets.
engineering_relevance: This helps practitioners choose and test optimizer components for QAOA, QML, QCNN, and VQE workloads while accounting for parameter count, measurement cost, and hardware constraints.
method: Benchmarks gradient-based, stochastic, and derivative-free optimizers in a modular setup.
Tests on QAOA MaxCut, Iris classification, QCNN binary MNIST, and VQE for H2.
Compares simulator and 156-qubit hardware runs using finite-shot evaluations and separate cost accounting.
evidence_signal: The study reports terminal and best objective values, post-training accuracies, and selected trajectories; simulator results are averaged over three seeds, while hardware runs use a real 156-qubit processor.
watch_item: The hardware experiments do not support an optimizer ranking or a causal claim about device noise.
paper_title: Benchmarking Modular Optimization Strategies for Parameterized Quantum Circuits
